records.name: Risaralda
records.current_summary: No department-specific legal, enforcement or incident finding was located for this division; the 2025 national reporting flags it neither for a public-order regime nor for territorial expansion of anti-LGBTIQ+ violence. It otherwise inherits national conditions.

sources.claim: English-language report (14 Apr 2025) on the murder of trans woman Sara Millerey, 32, in Bello, Antioquia (4 Apr 2025): beaten and thrown into a creek in daylight while bystanders filmed instead of helping; her death went viral 5 April, prompting vigils in several cities and a presidential order to investigate; the town's LGBTQ council co-director said it was the third LGBTQ killing there that year; 13 trans people were killed nationally in Q1 2025.

'We are killed for what we are' (30 Jul 2024): trans women in Caquetá threatened by armed groups after flyers announced a 'social cleansing' campaign naming 'faggots, lesbians and men and women who destroy homes' as targets; a trans woman was given a week to leave town or be killed and fled; more than 40 trans women were killed the previous year (41 in 2023, 8 between Feb-Apr 2024); activists document sexual violence by armed groups against trans women, including former combatant recruitment.

flags: the 2025 national reporting flags it neither for a public-order regime nor for territorial expansion of anti-LGBTIQ+ violence (the 2025 national report cited is among NO audited source)

records.name: Putumayo
records.current_summary: Like several frontier departments, this division operates under an  orden público  regime in which armed groups rather than the departmental police effectively regulate day-to-day conduct; a 2025 national LGBTIQ+ report documents the territorial expansion of violence against LGBTIQ+ people and the insufficiency of the state response, with trans women displaced from their regions by the same armed actors that displace others. Otherwise it inherits national conditions — no department-specific enforcement or incident data was located.

records.name: Guaviare
records.current_summary: No department-specific legal, enforcement or incident finding was located for this division; the 2025 national reporting flags it neither for a public-order regime nor for territorial expansion of anti-LGBTIQ+ violence. It otherwise inherits national conditions.

sources.claim: CNN 'As Equals' investigation (6 Aug 2025): armed groups in northern Colombia posted flyers carrying kill lists threatening 'homosexuals, lesbians, rapists, trans' (Guajira flyer, March 2024); only 3 of 155 criminal investigations into LGBTQ killings reached a verdict last year (about 2%, against a 9% overall homicide-conviction rate); nearly 50 queer and trans people killed this year to date; traces the history of 'social cleansing' campaigns and the gang alliance that enforces social order in the Medellín area, including expulsion of gay and trans residents.

'We are killed for what we are' (30 Jul 2024): trans women in Caquetá threatened by armed groups after flyers announced a 'social cleansing' campaign naming 'faggots, lesbians and men and women who destroy homes' as targets; a trans woman was given a week to leave town or be killed and fled; more than 40 trans women were killed the previous year (41 in 2023, 8 between Feb-Apr 2024); activists document sexual violence by armed groups against trans women, including former combatant recruitment.

flags: 'the 2025 national reporting flags it neither for a public-order regime nor for territorial expansion of anti-LGBTIQ+ violence' (absence-claim about national reporting absent from sources)

records.name: Arauca
records.current_summary: This department lies in the country's frontier 'orden publico' belt, where armed groups rather than departmental police effectively regulate conduct; regional reporting documents trans women displaced from frontier departments because of their gender identity, amid territorial expansion of anti-LGBTIQ violence nationally (one LGBTIQ+ person killed every 32 hours in 2025, 63% up on 2024). No department-specific legal or enforcement deviation beyond national homicide counts; risk assessed on the national framework.

sources.claim: News feature (14 Apr 2025): the transphobic murder of Sara Millerey, 32, a trans woman, in Bello, Antioquia - her fractured body dumped in a creek and a crowd filmed her drowning; the town had three LGBTQ murders in Q1 2025 and 13 trans people were killed nationally in Q1 2025; the president ordered an urgent investigation.

News report (30 Jul 2024): trans women in the department of Caquetá targeted by armed groups - Tatiana Cespedes, 51, given one week to leave town or be killed; 'social cleansing' flyers and WhatsApp messages circulated; 41 trans women killed nationally in 2023 and 8 between Feb-Apr 2024; armed groups still operating despite the 2016 peace accord.

'frontier orden publico belt, where armed groups rather than departmental police effectively regulate conduct' - no source mentions Arauca

The killings didn't stop there': documents the continuing wave of killings of queer and trans people in Colombia after the Bello murder, and the framing that in parts of Colombia being queer means 'to sign your own death sentence'. National-context source; mostly a video/interactive feature with limited extractable body text.

The Guardian (30 July 2024), 'We are killed for what we are': trans women in Colombia targeted by armed groups — armed groups in Caquetá circulated flyers threatening a 'social cleansing' of trans women as military targets; a trans woman with a salon was given a week to leave town; more than 40 trans women killed the previous year and 41 in 2023; armed-group displacement of trans women documented. National-pattern source relevant to intercity/border travel risk, not Huila-specific.

records.name: Puno
records.current_summary: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score.

sources.claim: Infobae Peru (20 Feb 2025): Congress's Women and Family Commission unanimously approved a bill barring trans people from public restrooms of the sex other than their birth sex (bills 6506 and 8457, by two governing-bloc legislators), with exceptions for custody situations, medical care, and accompanying elderly, under-12 or disabled people; the initiative also requires removing restroom signage ambiguous about who may enter. Trigger was a July 2023 complaint about gendered toilet labels at Lima's international airport. National law - applies in Puno as everywhere; still requires full plenary approval.

IDEHPUCP human-rights institute analysis (15 April 2025), 'Legalised discrimination': on 2 April 2025 Congress's plenary approved, waiving a second vote, the children's-sexual-rights law, fused by the Women and Family Commission with the trans bathroom-restriction bills; critiques the measure as institutionalised discrimination against trans people under national human-rights standards.
